bbox.description: The block's FIRST rectangle. Where the block's text crosses a column or page break it occupies several, and this is only the one its opening sits in — see `regions` for all of them.

regions.description: Every rectangle this block's text occupies, in reading order, as the converter states them. `page` and `bbox` above are the first entry. Absent or empty means NOT RECORDED — a map written before regions existed — and never that the block has no continuation; a reader that finds it empty falls back to the single rectangle.

page.description: 1-based page this rectangle is on. A block crossing a page break has entries with different pages, so the block-level `page` describes only its opening.

char_start.description: Offset into the block's text where this rectangle's content begins, inclusive. This is what orders the regions: y-coordinates cannot, because a continuation is usually higher up the page than the opening it follows (the top of the next column).

char_end.description: Offset into the block's text where this rectangle's content ends, exclusive.

converter.description: ingest backend that produced this map, e.g. 'pymupdf' or 'docling 2.x'

declared_title.description: the title the PDF declares in its own metadata (XMP / Info dictionary), verbatim and unjudged. Absent on maps written before it was recorded; empty means the file declares none, never that the paper has none. Whether it is title-shaped is decided by models.paper_title, not here.

source_sha256.description: sha256 of the PDF bytes this map was built from. `doc` cannot serve as an identity: a cited source is stored as <slug>.pdf, so every source map in a case names a different paper the same way. Absent on maps written before content hashing; absent means unknown, never 'matches'.

table_warnings.description: Fidelity warnings the table converter raised while reading this file, verbatim. A cell it could not place is text missing from the document. THREE answers: a list of messages (something was lost), [] (the converter was watched and lost nothing), and null (nobody watched — a map written before this was recorded, or a backend with no table model). null must never be read as "nothing was lost".
